request.prompt: These are 9 consecutive axial slices (superior to inferior, 1.25 mm spacing) from a chest CT, cropped to a 64 mm field of view centred on one structure in the lung. Is the structure at the centre of the images a pulmonary nodule or a cross-section of a blood vessel? Answer with one word, Nodule or Vessel, then one short sentence of reasoning, then the estimated diameter in mm.

content.text:
I don't actually see any images attached to your message, so I can't make this call — and guessing would be wrong either way.

If you re-send the slices, here's exactly what I'd look for:

- **Nodule:** a roughly round opacity that appears, reaches a maximum diameter in the central slices, and disappears symmetrically over the stack, without tubular continuity into adjacent slices.
- **Vessel:** a structure that stays similar in size across many slices, elongates, branches, or can be traced as a tube connecting toward the hilum; in-plane vessels look linear rather than round.

Please attach the images and I'll give you the one-word answer plus an estimated diameter in mm.
